root_cause: ServerSentEvent (pydantic model in fastapi/sse.py) validated only that 'id' had no NUL char; 'event' and 'id' accepted strings containing \r or \n, which format_sse_event writes verbatim as 'event: ...'/'id: ...' lines, so a multi-line value injects extra SSE fields/events on the wire.
best_solution:
Add a shared validator _check_single_line(v, field_name) that raises ValueError(f"SSE '{field_name}' must be a single line") if v contains '' or '
'. Wrap it as _check_event_single_line (AfterValidator on the 'event' field) and rename _check_id_no_null to _check_id_valid, which keeps the NUL check and then returns _check_single_line(v, 'id'). Update the Doc strings. The message follows the file's existing convention "SSE 'id' must not contain null characters" (quoted field name, one message per field). Checking  and 
 separately covers 
,  and 
, the three SSE line terminators. format_sse_event and the rest of the module are left alone.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_sse.py::test_server_sent_event_single_line_fields_reject_newlines, parametrized over field_name in {event, id} x value in {'first\nsecond','first\rsecond','first\r\nsecond'}: ServerSentEvent(data='test', **{field: value}) must raise ValueError (pydantic ValidationError is fine) with pytest.raises(match="SSE '<field_name>' must be a single line"). So the exact per-field message string is required. Existing tests in the same module (null-id rejection, format_sse_event, keepalive/_PING_INTERVAL imports used by fastapi.routing) must still collect and pass.
locating_signals: Statement names 'Server Sent Event' and the fields `id` and `event` plus 'multi-line content'. grep for ServerSentEvent / sse leads to fastapi/sse.py, where the existing _check_id_no_null AfterValidator on 'id' shows the pattern to extend. No function is named in the statement, and the error message string is not given.
our_outcome_summary: Failed in all four configs (v4/v6/v7/v8); every patch that existed broke test collection before any assertion ran. v4: the right idea (a _check_no_newlines AfterValidator on event and id) but it also rewrote format_sse_event (changed the return from bytes to str, reordered fields) and deleted KEEPALIVE_COMMENT and _PING_INTERVAL, so fastapi.routing failed with ImportError: cannot import name '_PING_INTERVAL'. It also changed the docstring '\\0' to '\0'. v6: empty patch after 110 calls. v7: the edit dropped the '] = None' that closes the 'event' Annotated, so SyntaxError: '[' was never closed. v8: added AfterValidator(_check_no_newlines) to both fields but never defined the function, so NameError at import. Even with clean edits, all three used a generic message ('SSE fields 'event' and 'id' must not contain newline characters' / 'SSE fields must not contain...' / 'SSE field must not contain...') that does not match the hidden regex "SSE 'event' must be a single line". Each also wrote its own tests/test_sse_validation.py instead of extending tests/test_sse.py.
acceptable_alternatives: Any validator setup (a field_validator on both fields, or separate AfterValidators) passes as long as event and id both reject \r and \n and the ValueError message contains exactly "SSE '<field>' must be a single line" for each field. Stacking a separate newline validator on id next to the existing null check is fine.
generalizable_lesson: When adding a validation error, copy the wording pattern of the neighbouring existing error messages (here "SSE 'id' must not contain null characters" becomes "SSE '<field>' must ..."), write one message per field with the field name in it, and reuse the statement's own words ('multi-line' becomes 'must be a single line'). Hidden tests often regex-match the message. Also make the smallest possible edit: never rewrite or truncate unrelated functions or module constants, and after every edit run an import or collection smoke test on the existing test module (python -c 'import pkg'; pytest --collect-only tests/test_<module>.py). That would have caught the NameError, SyntaxError and ImportError that sank all three non-empty patches.
